title: Apply skill-suite audit recommendations to council, subagent-swarm, and sprint-orchestration
description:
## Summary
Apply the audit's recommendations to the three multi-agent orchestration skills (`council`, `subagent-swarm`, `sprint-orchestration`) after independent review, and fix the shared-contract duplication between them with one canonical contract file.

## User Mandate
> "Review these audits of our skills within this repo and after careful consideration and independent review/analysis, make the appropriate changes and improvements as you see fit"

STRICT. The attached audit text is the input evidence, not a verbatim order; each recommendation must be applied, or explicitly dispositioned with a stated reason. Surface any deviation before applying it.

## Scope
- `council/SKILL.md`: replace the float confidence score with evidence provenance + a required blind-spot declaration; add a synthesizer tie-break rule (no averaging; define a discriminating check and make it the evidence gate; escalate when undecidable); require an assumption ledger; add the anti-pattern that agreement is not evidence.
- `subagent-swarm/SKILL.md`: add the one-writer rule for core Unity project files; define the reconciler toolkit (unified diffs / patch files, not re-typed code); add the failure branch.
- `sprint-orchestration/SKILL.md` + `assets/sequential-sprint-handoff-template.md`: add the council evidence-gate provenance rule (proportional), the validation-failure rollback protocol, the assumption-ledger requirement, and failure/abort rows.
- New `.github/instructions/agent-orchestration-contract.instructions.md`: one canonical shared contract (workflow map, repo contract, assumption ledger, blind-spot declaration, rollback protocol, evidence provenance) that all three skills cite instead of restating.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each recommendation in the supplied audit maps to an applied edit or a recorded disposition with a reason.
- The three skills no longer restate the full repo contract independently; each cites the canonical contract file and keeps only the load-bearing rules inline.
- The rollback protocol forbids destructive whole-worktree resets and restores only the failed round's or stream's paths, consistent with the BeastMaster invariant "Do not revert unrelated worktree changes".
- No code, runtime, or task JSON is edited by hand.
- `git diff` shows only the intended `.github/` guidance changes.

## Validation
- Read each target file before and after the edit; confirm the applied text matches the intent and no `(.github/)` content changed unintentionally.
- `git diff --check` passes; `git diff --stat` lists only `.github/` paths.
- Confirm the canonical contract is referenced from all three skills.
- Run `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` after creating this record; expect zero collisions and zero skipped files.

## Findings
- Confirmed: `council/SKILL.md` step 3 required "Confidence from 0.0 to 1.0" and the report template had a numeric confidence column; no seat-level blind-spot field existed.
- Confirmed: the audit's claim that no rollback branch exists is correct — `sprint-orchestration` step 4 reviews the diff but has no failure path, and `subagent-swarm` step 4 says "merges outputs" without a mechanism.
- Confirmed: the full repo contract is restated inline in `sprint-orchestration` only, while `subagent-swarm` and `council` restate fragments; that duplication is the maintenance risk the audit names.
- Repo evidence that council consensus is not evidence: `docs/audits/audit-sdf-sampler-race-2026-09-11.md` — a 14-seat council recorded the SDF sampler scratch race as fixed; the fix does not isolate scratch (`TSK-0212`, `TSK-0198`).
- Deliberate deviation from the audit: "Only accept tasks that have passed a Council evidence gate" is applied only to council-derived or high-impact rounds. Ordinary bounded rounds keep one executable acceptance check, because a blanket council gate would contradict the skill's own fit check and degrade fast.

## Blockers
None.

## Next Step
Edit the three skills, add the canonical contract file, validate, and record evidence.

comments.body:
## Implementation + validation evidence (2026-09-13)

`git diff --stat` (tracked): 5 files, +242/-49, all under `.github/`; plus one new untracked file `.github/instructions/agent-orchestration-contract.instructions.md` (101 lines).

### Applied — council
- Removed the `0.0`–`1.0` seat confidence score and the numeric column in the report template. Replaced with per-claim evidence provenance (`re-run` / `spot-checked` / `report-only`) plus a required blind-spot declaration (`Cannot guarantee: <claim> without <file, test, or Unity run>`).
- Added the synthesizer tie-breaking rule: on disagreement, do not average or blend; define one concrete Unity test or static check that discriminates, and make it the prerequisite evidence gate. If none can discriminate, keep both options and escalate to the user. Added a matching Decision Branch.
- Added seat-independence mechanics: write each seat before reading the next; a later seat may not revise an earlier finding.
- Added the anti-pattern with repo evidence: a seat claiming a defect is handled must supply the discriminating test; the 14-seat council that recorded the SDF sampler scratch race as fixed was wrong (`docs/audits/audit-sdf-sampler-race-2026-09-11.md`, `TSK-0212`, `TSK-0198`).
- Added the assumption ledger requirement, section 8 (Hand Off), and updated Outcome / Completion Checks / Quality Bar / References.

### Applied — subagent-swarm
- One-writer rule: while a stream mutates `Assets/`, `ProjectSettings/`, `Packages/`, `.csproj`, `.slnx`, or `.asmdef`, no other stream may; others are read-only and emit patches.
- Reconciler toolkit defined: unified diffs / patch files per stream, applied one at a time with the focused gate re-run after each; the coordinator must not re-type code into context.
- Failure branch: a contradicting or failing stream is quarantined, not merged; rollback per the contract.
- Added Workflow Position, assumption ledger + blind-spot in Gather Evidence, per-claim provenance in Stage D, failure Decision Point, and a References section (previously absent).

### Applied — sprint-orchestration + handoff template
- Sprint Setup step 3 adds round gate classification: **Council-gated** (link the report, adopt its evidence gate verbatim) or **Bounded** (one executable acceptance check). Recorded in the round log and the template's new Gate class column.
- Step 4 adds the explicit failure branch: stop, do not commit, restore only the round's paths to the recorded fixed-point SHA, re-brief; two failures on the same gate means re-scope, not retry. Do Not and the template repeat the prohibition.
- Translated the vague `report-trusted` / `independently re-run` tiers into the canonical `report-only` / `spot-checked` / `re-run` names, with an explicit note that provenance is not task validation state (owned by `task-tracker`).
- Brief Contents now requires the assumption ledger and per-claim provenance; the inline Shared Repo Contract keeps only the load-bearing rules and points at the canonical contract.
- Template: fixed point marked as the rollback target, Gate class parameter, per-round failure/rollback rows, no-destructive-reset rule.

### Applied — canonical contract (new)
`.github/instructions/agent-orchestration-contract.instructions.md` now owns the workflow map (council -> sprint -> swarm -> creature-workflow), the repo contract, the assumption ledger, the blind-spot declaration, evidence provenance, and the rollback protocol. `council`, `subagent-swarm`, `sprint-orchestration`, and `BeastMaster.agent.md` cite it instead of restating it. `sprint-orchestration` was also added to BeastMaster's graduated discovery (it was previously not listed).

### Deliberate deviations (surfaced, not silent)
1. **Council gate is proportional, not blanket.** The audit asked that `sprint-orchestration` "only accept tasks that have passed a Council evidence gate". That is applied to council- or audit-derived and high-impact rounds. Ordinary bounded rounds keep one executable acceptance check, because a blanket gate contradicts the skill's own fit check and would make the triad unusable for routine work. Class is recorded per round.
2. **Rollback is scoped, not `git reset --hard`.** The audit's proposed hard reset was rejected: it would destroy unrelated worktree changes, which the BeastMaster invariant forbids. The protocol instead restores only the failed round's or stream's paths to the recorded fixed-point SHA (`git restore --source=<sha> -- <paths>` + delete created files) and explicitly bans `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd`, and `git checkout .`. This achieves the audit's goal (no polluted worktree poisoning the next iteration) without data loss.

### Validation performed
- Read every target file before and after each edit; applied text matches the intent above.
- `git status --short -- .github`: only the 5 intended modifications plus the new `instructions/` directory. No code, runtime, or task JSON touched.
- `git diff --check -- .github`: exit 0 (no whitespace errors).
- `Test-Path` on all 11 cross-referenced targets (contract, three skills, handoff template, agent, `Assets/Scripts/README.md`, `task-tracker`, `unity-validation`, `creature-workflow`, `cc-audit-synthesis`): all exist. Relative paths resolve from each skill's directory.
- `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1`: `Fixed: 0  Skipped: 0`. Task-board integrity gate passes; TSK-0255 allocated without collision.
- No Unity gate required: documentation-only change, no code or serialized-data edit.

### Residual risk
- On-demand discovery of the new instruction file by the harness is not directly verifiable from here. Access is guaranteed by the explicit path references in the three skills and the agent file, which is the primary route.
- Advisory-only enforcement: the new rules are prose in skills, not hooks. A future deterministic hook could enforce the rollback and one-writer rules mechanically.
